title: Nicholas (6 December)
hook: a bishop who secretly gave dowries to three poor girls, the root of Santa Claus

segments.voice: Yesterday, Andrew, who spent an afternoon with Jesus and went home to get his brother. Your line was he brought his brother.

A bag of gold sails through an open window in the dark and lands on the floor of a poor man's house. Nobody sees who threw it. The man has three daughters and no money for their dowries, and in that world, the story says, it meant they had no good future ahead of them. Now one of them can marry. A while later, another bag comes through the window. Then the father decides he has to know. He waits up, and he catches a man at the window: Nicholas.
screen: `GOLD THROUGH A DARK WINDOW.` → `THREE DAUGHTERS, NO DOWRY.` → `THE FATHER WAITS UP.`

segments.voice: Nicholas was a bishop of Myra, a town on the southern coast of what is now Turkey. Very little is known for certain about his life. What came down instead is a set of stories, and the dowry story is the one that stuck. In the telling, Nicholas has inherited money and wants to help the family without being seen. So he goes at night, three times. On the third night the father runs out and catches him, and falls at his feet. And Nicholas asks him for one thing: tell no one. That request is the heart of it. Jesus says it in the Sermon on the Mount. In the Douay-Rheims: "But when thou dost alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth." And the promise that follows: "thy Father who seeth in secret will repay thee." Nicholas wanted the gift to be all gift. There's a small irony here. The father clearly didn't keep the secret, or we'd never have heard it. And the secret giver ended up with a very public afterlife. In the Netherlands he became Sinterklaas, and the usual account traces Santa Claus to that Dutch name. In parts of Europe, children still set out shoes on the eve of his feast and find small gifts in them by morning. Under the red suit and the reindeer is a bishop at a window, throwing gold into the dark and hoping not to be seen.
screen: `A BISHOP OF MYRA.` · `THREE NIGHTS, AND THEN: TELL NO ONE.` · `LET NOT THY LEFT HAND KNOW.` · `FROM SINTERKLAAS TO SANTA CLAUS.` · then, large: `THY FATHER WHO SEETH IN SECRET.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who could use a lift right now: not a grand gesture, but coffee paid for, a note left on a desk, a bill quietly covered, a chore done before anyone wakes up. Choose one, work out how it could be done so they never find out it was you, and notice how it feels to give up the thank-you in advance. If you pray, offer the gift to God before you give it.
Nicholas. The bishop of Myra who threw dowries through a poor man's window at night, asked to stay unknown, and became the root of Santa Claus.
Your line: in secret. A gift that's all gift, with no thank-you note coming back. Go gently.

howItsDone: Saint Nicholas is remembered on 6 December; in parts of Europe children set out shoes or stockings the night before and find small gifts in the morning, and some parishes collect gifts for the poor around his feast.
